note: For each domain: the eight workflow steps and the performed and owned conditions for each of the eight judgment axes. Items, results and evidence input all read this one file. `verify_targets` and `artifacts` are what the result's action items draw on, so they must be concrete here to avoid vague wording

workflow.name: How the problem arrives
workflow.detail: Signal ranges and supply conditions required by a sensor or load arrive as a specification

workflow.name: Inputs received
workflow.detail: Input and output voltage and current, bandwidth, noise limits, operating temperature range

workflow.name: What gets decided first
workflow.detail: Circuit topology, type of active device, and which performance target to protect first

workflow.name: Methods used
workflow.detail: Operating point design, small-signal analysis, noise budget allocation, stability review

workflow.name: Tools used
workflow.detail: Circuit simulator, component datasheets, calculation sheets, test equipment

workflow.name: Deliverables produced
workflow.detail: Schematic, component selection table, design calculations, prototype board and measurements

workflow.name: What it is compared against
workflow.detail: Simulated values, datasheet limits, prototype board measurements, existing circuits

workflow.name: When it goes wrong
workflow.detail: When oscillation, saturation or excess noise appears, narrow the cause to component values, layout or supply

J1.l2: Wrote down what the circuit would cover, based on the given spec
J1.l3: Decided the functions and limits the circuit had to meet when there was no spec

J2.l2: Turned the requirements into gain, bandwidth and noise figures
J2.l3: Set priorities between conflicting noise and current-draw targets

J3.l2: Set component values and the bias operating point
J3.l3: Allocated the noise budget and margins based on what each function needed

J4.l2: Checked the operating point and frequency response in a circuit simulator
J4.l3: Backed up the simulation results separately with hand calculations

J5.l2: Delivered the schematic and component selection table
J5.l3: A prototype board was built from that schematic

J6.l3: Judged the design by checking datasheet limits against design margins

J7.l2: Changed component values after running into oscillation or saturation
J7.l3: Narrowed the cause to components, layout or supply and stopped it from recurring

J8.l2: Presented the schematic at a design review
J8.l3: That circuit went onto a product board
